hypothesis: msgsettle's reported ~20ms fresh-session first-turn auth-lock contention retry (crates/pa-core/src/auth/storage.rs acquire_lock, TS-parity 'acquireLockSyncWithRetry: 10 attempts, 20ms apart') is an in-process race between two worker threads (the admission thread right after the durable user-row append vs the turn thread's from-scratch model-resolution registry build), both calling AuthStorage::create -> FileAuthStorageBackend::with_lock; the TS product runs its sync auth lock single-threaded, so same-process contention is a Rust-port artifact and a process-local per-path mutex can remove the 20ms class with byte-identical cross-process retry semantics.
approach: Baseline decomposition first (no code changes): 29 fresh-session trials on one VM at origin/rust 4ed68f6e9 (fresh dir/daemon/session per trial; bench compare.msg_send mock-regime protocol replicated verbatim incl. 120x40 PTY, probe-input-ready, typed prompt, Enter->first-chunk ack, needle+600ms-stability settle; PI_REQUEST_TIMING on for phase extraction) + 3 strace -f diagnostic trials (syscall timeline only) with mkdir/rmdir/utimensat/rename/fsync added to the trace filter. Then candidate = in-process serialization of FileAuthStorageBackend::with_lock (one commit, +37/-2, crates/pa-core/src/auth/storage.rs only); lane folded to origin/rust 61d92a206 (post-fold re-diff = exactly the one file); ABBA paired legs base(61d92a206) vs cand(34a6ba359) on the same VM: LEGF 8/arm fresh 1-turn + LEGW 4/arm 2-turn (turn2 = warm contrast), arms interleaved A-B-B-A per round, binary sha asserted per trial, session-row parity oracle across arms, 2 cand strace diagnostics. I/O regime: fleet advisory v0.9 preflight (>=40 isolated fresh+sync_all+rename at 0.5s spacing + >=20 repeat-fsync; H/M/D by stall-rate/max/baseline-p50) before every leg.
parity_notes: Frozen parity untouched: the file protocol (proper-lockfile mkdir/utimensat/stale-reclaim), the 10x20ms retry structure, settings storage, session JSONL, RLM wire, prompts, TUI behavior all unchanged; the patch adds ONLY a process-local Mutex<()> per auth document path taken around the existing critical section. Cross-process contention keeps identical retry semantics (the cand strace residual class: 2 retry sleeps in 16 turns, ZERO same-process racing pairs - the lock was held by the untraced TUI process). Session rows byte-identical in type/role/content-shape sequences across arms. The measured mock path (prime-inference/mock-1 via bench vendored mock_provider SSE, queue-matched script) replicates the campaign's compare.msg_send provider path. The driver's typed prompt carries the probe-prefix leftover 'Zq7' exactly as the bench harness's own erase_all semantics leave it (bench core/harness.py erase_all stops when the full token is gone) - same protocol class as every msg_send row; disclosed.

outcome: POSITIVE, mechanism confirmed and fixed at its layer: the ~20ms fresh-session first-turn class (and the warm-turn admission variant) is same-process auth.json.lock contention between the admission thread and the turn thread's from-scratch model-resolution registry build - a Rust-port artifact (TS runs its sync auth lock single-threaded, so its 10x20ms retry only ever fires cross-process). A process-local per-path mutex around FileAuthStorageBackend::with_lock's existing critical section removes it: dispatch slow-class 8/16 -> 2/16, submit->assistant_row p50 26.3 -> 8.28ms (-18.0ms, -68%), submit->reply_visible p50 51.65 -> 29.85ms on the folded tip, with byte-identical cross-process retry semantics (the residual 2 slow turns are TUI-vs-worker cross-process contention, TS-parity by design). No parity surface touched: one file, +37/-2.
decision: Lane evidence complete at folded tip 61d92a206; PR opened for numeric review + both adversarial reviewers on the final PR SHA. The 20ms-class disappearance claim is scoped to same-process contention; cross-process contention (rare; TUI auth reads) retains the TS-parity retry by design. Reported-only findings: (1) auth.json is lock-cycled ~36x per fresh first turn (daemon+worker surfaces rebuild AuthStorage per call) - a consolidation candidate for a future lane, parity-sensitive (per-call rebuild is the documented R8 behavior); (2) the residual warm-turn ack->user_row spread (0.9-26.8ms) includes the durable-append fdatasync (~0.5ms typical) - flush-regime sensitive per the fleet advisory.
